posts.contentHtml:
In the US state of Texas, propane gas powers many parts of daily life, including home and water heating, cooking and refrigerating food, clothes drying, running farm and industrial equipment, and manufacturing plastics and other compounds.

This guide covers everything you need to know about propane services in Texas, including what they are, what they do, and the licenses required to operate in this state. At Action Propane, Inc., we provide full-service propane services across Leander, Austin, and the greater Central Texas area.

What Are Propane Services in Texas?

Propane services in Texas are licensed companies that distribute propane gas from production sites to distribution terminals via pipeline, truck, barge, railroad, or tanker ship. Propane marketers fill their trucks at the terminals and deliver propane to end users.

What Does a Propane Gas Company in Texas Do?

To meet the energy needs of homes and businesses, a propane gas company in Texas handles the following operations:

  • Propane Delivery – Transporting propane gas or cylinders from one location to another. Knowing the signs you need immediate propane delivery in Austin helps you avoid running out.
  • Propane Installation – Installing a propane tank aboveground or underground based on your property's needs. Our guide to choosing the right propane tank installer in Texas explains exactly what to look for.
  • Propane Maintenance – Repairing or upgrading faulty propane systems through professional servicing. Ongoing propane system service and repair keeps your equipment safe and efficient.

You can explore our full range of propane services for homes and businesses across Central Texas.

Licensing Requirements for a Propane Company in Texas

Here are the major licensing categories a propane company in Texas may need to run its business:

  • Category A-1: License for assembling, repairing, installing, testing, and selling ASME containers.
  • Category A-2: License for assembling, repairing, installing, testing, and selling DOT cylinders.
  • Category B: License for transporting propane, installing and repairing transport systems, and testing LP-gas storage containers.
  • Category C: License for transporting LP-gas, installing and repairing transport systems, and loading and unloading LP-gas.
  • Category D: License for general installers and repairmen.

Frequently Asked Questions

How often should a propane furnace be serviced? Most manufacturers recommend servicing a propane furnace once a year, ideally before the heating season, to keep it running safely and efficiently.

Who services propane fireplaces? A licensed propane company like Action Propane can inspect, service, and repair propane fireplaces along with your other propane appliances.

How long can a propane cylinder stay in service? DOT propane cylinders must be requalified 12 years after manufacture and periodically thereafter. A licensed supplier can inspect and exchange cylinders as needed.

posts.excerpt: Planning a residential propane tank installation? Explore 4 key factors, including safety, location, and tank size, for a seamless installation process.
posts.contentHtml:
Planning a residential propane tank installation in Central Texas? It's not as simple as it looks, especially the first time. Before you install a propane gas tank for your home, there are four key factors to get right, from code compliance to tank size and placement. Here's what Leander and greater Austin homeowners need to know about professional propane tank installation.

1. Follow NFPA Guidelines and Local Codes

Always check local laws first. Propane tanks must comply with NFPA 58 (National Fire Protection Association) standards, which govern tank placement, clearances, and safety distances from your home and property lines. A licensed installer will make sure your setup passes inspection.

2. Choose the Right Tank Size and Type

Tanks range from roughly 100 to 1,000+ pounds, and capacity depends on your property size and usage. As a rule of thumb, a 2,200-square-foot home may use 1,200-1,500 gallons of propane per year. Picking the right size up front prevents frequent refills and keeps costs predictable. Once your tank is in place, scheduled residential propane delivery helps you plan refills and avoid running low.

3. Decide Between Above-Ground and Underground

You'll choose between an above-ground propane tank and an underground tank. Above-ground tanks are easier and cheaper to install and service; underground tanks save yard space and look cleaner. Your choice affects both installation cost and long-term maintenance. Whichever you choose, ongoing propane system service and repair protects your investment and keeps the system safe.

4. Confirm Your Home Appliances Are Propane-Ready

Make sure every appliance is properly configured for propane to avoid fire risk or carbon monoxide issues. Always use licensed professionals for appliance conversions and hookups. If you are weighing propane for a new home, review our guide to affordable propane heating solutions for homes and businesses to understand the long-term value.

How much does propane tank installation cost? Cost depends on tank size and whether it's above-ground or underground. Underground installations cost more due to excavation, but offer a cleaner look. Call us for a quote tailored to your Central Texas property.

How long does a propane tank installation take? Most above-ground residential installations can be completed in a single visit once permits and site prep are handled. Underground installs take longer because of excavation.
